ONE CARD, FROM THE ORDER-BOOK LANE, AND IT IS THE ONLY ONE OF THE DAY'S TEN CANDIDATES THAT SURVIVED READING ITS OWN FILINGS. The government lane kept nothing out of 34 PIB releases - the four Cabinet decisions it did surface were a Rs 12.6 lakh crore MICRO-CREDIT GUARANTEE ceiling, a routine twice-yearly fertiliser subsidy rate-fixing, a Rs 4,111 cr entrepreneurship credit scheme and a Rs 3,230 cr museum with no named contractor. Only the museum is an order book at all, and nothing in the band can be attached to it from a document, so nothing was mapped. The commodity lane is the day's weak point and the reason is measurable: wpi_month is still 2026-04, SEVEN MONTHS STALE, and the WPI series drives the top of the strength table, so crude at +10.70 and silver at +10.16 are April readings dressed as today's. No card was published off a WPI-led signal. The strongest trade-led signal, tungsten at +10.00, has an empty beneficiary list, and the search it triggered ended in a document-backed NON-addition: Diffusion Engineers is the only tungsten-exposed name in the band and its own FY26 annual report says it refuses to hold speculative tungsten inventory, which makes it a sufferer, not a beneficiary - so the map gained evidence and no name.

The filings lane produced Jyoti Structures at score 9 (+20.0% on 15.2x volume), but it is already published, so its bank-guarantee unlock went in as an update, not a card. DCX Systems looked like a candidate on filing COUNT and turned out to have H1 revenue down 42%. Frontier Springs grew 20.5% in the quarter, short of the 30% tier. Gala Precision's '44% order book growth' is quarterly INFLOW, not a book total.

That left Texmaco Rail, and the interesting part of it is a correction. The screen said the order book rose 56.8%; the real figure on the company's own consolidated definition is 71.8%, because the screen had picked up a slide total that excludes the subsidiaries and JVs - one PDF carries THREE different order-book totals for 30-Sep-2026 (Rs 10,940 cr, Rs 9,983 cr, Rs 9,679 cr). The honest card is not a bull case: Rs 5,327 cr of that Rs 10,940 cr book, 49% of it, is two Letters of Award from ONE private South African counterparty pair, the larger loco leg conditional on a definitive agreement no filing confirms has been signed; standalone revenue fell 31.3% in the quarter; Indian Railways has gone from 65% of the book in FY23 to 1% now; consolidated Q2 profit is mostly a Rs 76 cr one-off on diluting a leasing JV; and two CFOs resigned in seven weeks. It is published at medium confidence with no forward EPS, because a forward EPS here would be a number about an unsigned contract.
